selection: Curated (audits of 2026-10-20). The first three prompts of the older fig:qual_main were viewed whole and at native pixels and all three were replaced; the medieval square that then took the middle row was replaced in turn (see 'replaced'). Eligible: the 195 evaluation prompts minus the four development prompts, the prompts of Figure 1 and every prompt displayed in another figure (galleries as displayed, showcase, ablation, failures, progressive). Rule: shortlist by SCA's ImageReward and MUSIQ_c percentiles within its own 195 images (eval/a4k195_main), keeping prompts where AReA and HRDiT each have ImageReward and HPSv2.1 at or above their own 25th percentile (asserted for every row; full attention is not constrained); view SCA whole and at native pixels and reject extra or repeated subjects, objects the prompt does not ask for, broken anatomy, seams, lattice or speckle; prefer varied subjects. The middle row was meant to show architecture or a street; every such candidate failed the viewing or the rule (see percentiles.rejected and percentiles.metric_stage), so it showed an interior still life, 2232973817337527860 (pink lilies in a vase by a paneled door). Its native pixels were clean; minor background quirks: a flat beige door with a brass knob and a wall plate beside the paneled door, and a squared back piece on the round table top; no subject is repeated. Clean at overview but not used, being a second landscape: 3638740675706761149. The rule constrains ImageReward and HPSv2.1 only; the baselines' MUSIQ_c percentiles are recorded in percentiles.shown. Ranking on SCA's metrics favours SCA in the printed values. None of the shown prompts is displayed in another figure. All of this ranked and viewed the published operator's images (sca_nb). On 2026-10-30 the SCA column switched to the final operator (sca_v2), the same prompts and seed; its images were viewed whole and at native pixels (final_operator.viewed) and its printed values come from eval/a4k195_main_sca_v2. The final operator's lily image streaks the table top, so the middle row was re-chosen on 2026-10-30 by the same rule on the final operator's metrics (eval/a4k195_main_sca_v2; the development prompts and every prompt shown in any figure excluded) with a native audit of every tile: the still life m947425340308551929 failed (see-through third bottle, floating pears) and the character at a desk m7824758602266642611 passed (its published-operator rejection does not hold for the final operator's image; percentiles.readmitted_final_operator). The other two rows were not re-ranked (their final-operator percentiles are in percentiles.shown).

crop_rule: Automatic, not hand-placed: fig_qual_main.auto_box over the drawn methods (area, hrdit and sca), i.e. the 432x240 (width x height) window with the largest mean PIL FIND_EDGES response of the 8x box-downsampled greyscale images, at least 256 px from every border. Over the four images used before review round 1 (full attention included) auto_box gives the same window in every row (asserted; examples[].crop_xywh_with_full_attention). The same window is cropped from every drawn method; layouts differ between methods, so the crops differ in content. Before review round 1 the window was 320x240 over all four methods.
metric: MUSIQ_c (CSV column musiq_crop1024): pyiqa MUSIQ averaged over four fixed random 1024^2 crops per image, crop positions set by the prompt id and shared across methods (Appendix app:metrics). It is a per-image score, not a score of the displayed window. Printed to one decimal; the best printed value per row is bold.
